mcqs.question: Which of the following statements correctly compares an infinite set with a finite set?

options.A: An infinite set always contains a finite set as a proper subset.
options.B: An infinite set has a larger cardinality than any finite set.
options.C: An infinite set can be put into a one-to-one correspondence with a proper subset of itself, whereas a finite set cannot.
options.D: An infinite set must contain all natural numbers.

mcqs.answer: An infinite set can be put into a one-to-one correspondence with a proper subset of itself, whereas a finite set cannot.
mcqs.explanation: A key property of infinite sets is that they can be mapped bijectively onto a proper subset of themselves (e.g., the set of natural numbers N and the set of even natural numbers). Finite sets lack this property because removing any element reduces their cardinality. Option C captures this defining comparison. Options A and D are not universally true, and option B, while true, does not express the distinctive comparison property.

mcqs.question: The set {7} is an example of which type of set?
mcqs.explanation: A singleton set contains exactly one element. The set {7} has precisely one element, 7, so it is a singleton set. It is also a finite set, but the most specific classification asked is "singleton set". Options A, C, and D are incorrect definitions for this set.

mcqs.question: Two sets A = {1, 2, 3} and B = {3, 2, 1} are ____.
mcqs.explanation: Equal sets have exactly the same elements, irrespective of order. Since A and B contain precisely the elements 1, 2, and 3, they are equal sets. Equivalent sets (option B) refer to having the same number of elements, which is also true but less specific. Options C and D are false.

mcqs.question: If set X = {a, b, c} and set Y = {1, 2, 3}, then X and Y are ____.
mcqs.explanation: Two sets are equivalent when they have the same number of elements, i.e., there exists a one-to-one correspondence between them. Both X and Y have three elements, so they are equivalent. They are not equal because their elements differ, nor are they subsets or disjoint.

mcqs.question: Which statement correctly defines the empty set?

options.A: A set containing no elements, denoted by ∅.
options.B: A set containing exactly one element.
options.C: A set with infinitely many elements.
options.D: A set that contains itself as an element.

mcqs.answer: A set containing no elements, denoted by ∅.
mcqs.explanation: The empty set, also called the null set, has no elements and is symbolized by ∅ or {}. Option A gives the precise definition. Option B describes a singleton set, C an infinite set, and D is a false statement (no set can contain itself in standard set theory).

mcqs.question: Which of the following is a finite set?

options.A: The set of all natural numbers
options.B: The set of all points on a line segment
options.D: The set of all real numbers between 0 and 1

mcqs.explanation: A finite set has a countable number of elements. The set {2,4,6,8} contains exactly four elements, making it finite. Options A, B, and D describe infinite collections.

mcqs.question: Which of the following is an example of an infinite set?
mcqs.explanation: The set of all prime numbers has no upper bound; there are infinitely many primes, so it is an infinite set. Option A has five elements, C has two, and D has one, all finite.

mcqs.question: A teacher writes down the name of each student who scores above 90 in a test. If only one student achieves this, the set of such students is ____.

options.C: Finite set with more than one element

mcqs.explanation: When exactly one element satisfies a condition, the resulting set contains that single element, making it a singleton set. It is not empty (A) because there is an element, nor is it larger (C) or infinite (D).
